text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- SPD Lower Saxony permier Gerhard Schoeder says the Social Democrats must sort out problems with their party programme, inspired by election victory of Britain's Labour Party
- SPD and tenants opposed to Construction Minister Klaus Toepfer's plans to reform state housing
- The federation of business consultants fears a new wave of companies folding after a change in insolvency regulations due to come into force in 1999
HANDELSBLATT
- The "German Tony Blair", SPD Lower Saxony premier Gerhard Schroeder, waits in the wings after election of British Labour Party inspired German counterpart, the Social Democrats
- Why the SPD is not New Labour
- Head of German Industry Federation says Britain is better equipt for globalisation than Germany
- Prosecutors are investigating possibly one of the biggest insider trading cases involving SAP employees
- Germany does not want to court confrontation, despite the fact that Iran has said the German ambassador in Tehran is no longer welcome and should not return to the country for the time being
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG

- SPD Schleswig-Holstein Premier Heidi Simonis calls on Social Democrats to nominate their chancellor candidate as soon as possible ahead of elections in 1998. Party debates its own direction after election success of British counterpart, Tony Blair's Labour Party
- Unemployment has dropped by 130,000
- Telekom is not planning to raise rates for standard information
DIE WELT

- The SPD rows over its direction. Lower Saxony premier Gerhard Schroeder says the party is in need of reform. The British election has prompted a debate in Germany about the leadership of Labour's German counterpart, the Social Democrats
- East Berlin's Stasi was behind attempted assassination of Saar premier Johannes Hoffmann in 1955
- Albanian President Sali Berisha said in interview with Die Welt that the new elections set for June were at risk
- SPD parliamentary leader Rudolf Scharping is prepared for more talks with coalition about tax reform
- Bonn rejects tough stance with Iran, after the country said the German ambassador in Tehran was not welcome for the time being
- Workers from German DGB trade union federation demonstrate for jobs and say token strikes are possible
